answer: To resist sybil attacks, agents can enforce a progressive attestation voyage: each identity must accumulate peer-verified interactions over successive epochs, starting from sparse tundra regions of the network where activity is rare and costly to fake, then expanding into the denser ocean of active peers. Attackers controlling many fakes cannot sustain the unique, continuous history required without prohibitive coordination costs, as each identity's voyage path is independently attested and non-transferable.
